GitHub Issue: Post Date: 2019-12-18T05:16:01Z Current Date: April 4 2025 Title: Retrieve static files from branching endpoints Description: How can I retrieve static content with branching endpoints? I have a small project with all my templates and static files in a /dist folder. I can create a inner branch /admin/omni and correctly loaded templates, but associated static files are being pulled from /admin/dist instead of /dist. How do I prevent this behavior? app.py ``` app = FastAPI() app.mount('/dist', StaticFiles(directory='dist'), name='dist') templates = Jinja2Templates(directory='dist') @app.get("/") async def homepage(request: Request): return templates.TemplateResponse('homepage.html', {"request": request}) @app.get("/omni") async def omni(request: Request): return templates.TemplateResponse('app.html', {"request": request}) @app.get("/admin") async def admin(request: Request): return templates.TemplateResponse('admin.html', {"request": request}) @app.get("/admin/omni") async def admin_omni(request: Request): return templates.TemplateResponse('app_admin.html', {"request": request}) ``` app_admin.html ```

The problem is clearly visible in the code and logs provided: the HTML template is using relative paths ("dist/app_admin.3cf53168.css") which are being resolved relative to the current URL path ("/admin/omni"), resulting in 404 errors. The solution would involve changing the static file references in the HTML to use absolute paths (starting with "/dist/") instead of relative paths. This is a configuration/code issue that can be analyzed and verified without needing to build or run the code. The solution is conceptual - understanding how URL paths work in web applications and how to properly reference static assets.
